# Copilot Instructions for this repository

Purpose: help Copilot CLI sessions understand how to build, run, and reason about this SvelteKit + Supabase project.

---

## Quick commands

- Install deps: `pnpm install` (or `npm install`)
- Dev server: `pnpm run dev` (alias: `npm run dev`)
- Build: `pnpm run build`
- Preview build: `pnpm run preview`
- Type check / validation: `pnpm run check` (use `check:watch` for iterative work)
- Lint: `pnpm run lint` (runs Prettier --check then ESLint)
- Format: `pnpm run format`

Run ESLint on a single file: `pnpm exec eslint path/to/file` (add `--fix` to auto-fix where applicable).

Tests: No test runner or tests are present in the repository currently.

---

## High-level architecture

- Tech stack: SvelteKit (Svelte 5, runes enabled), TypeScript, Vite. Project configured to deploy with the Vercel adapter.
- Entrypoints: main app code lives in `src/routes/` (primary UI in `src/routes/(main)`); shared UI/components under `src/lib/components`.
- Auth / data layer: Supabase is used for authentication and DB access via `@supabase/ssr`.
  - Server-side supabase client is created in `src/hooks.server.ts` and attached to `event.locals.supabase`.
  - The layout load (`src/routes/+layout.ts`) creates either a browser client or a server client and returns `{ supabase, claims }` to the UI.
  - Client-side layout (`src/routes/+layout.svelte`) subscribes to Supabase auth state and invalidates `supabase:auth` to trigger reloads.
- Data model: a `profiles` table is used for user profile data (see `src/routes/(main)/account/+page.server.ts` where `profiles` is selected/upserted).
- Routing pattern: routes in `(main)` are the authenticated/primary application; top-level routes expose public flows (login, auth callbacks, etc.).

---

## Key conventions and patterns

- Auth checks: use `supabase.auth.getClaims()` to validate and read JWT claims (preferred over `getSession` in this codebase). A missing or invalid `claims` value indicates no authenticated user.
- In server-side `load` functions that depend on authentication, call `depends('supabase:auth')` (see `+layout.ts`) so client-side auth changes can invalidate server data.
- On the client, call `invalidate('supabase:auth')` when receiving auth state changes to re-run server loads.
- Server client & cookies: `hooks.server.ts` wires a server client into `event.locals.supabase` and implements `cookies.setAll`/`getAll` behavior so Supabase can sync session cookies. Review this file when changing auth flows.
- Profile upserts: profile operations use `.from('profiles').upsert({ id: claims.sub, ... })` where `claims.sub` is the user id.
- Form actions: server form actions validate inputs on the server (e.g., password minimum length, password confirmation) and use `fail(...)` and `redirect(...)` per SvelteKit patterns.
- Magic links: magic-link sign-in uses `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { emailRedirectTo } })` with a redirect to `/auth/confirm`.
- Runes mode: Svelte compiler runes mode is enabled in `svelte.config.js` (project-wide) — follow rune-aware syntax in components.

---

## Where to look first for auth or profile issues

- `src/hooks.server.ts` — server client creation + cookie handling
- `src/routes/+layout.ts` — SSR/browser supabase client selection and `getClaims` usage
- `src/routes/+layout.svelte` — client auth change subscription + `invalidate` usage
- `src/routes/(main)/account/*` — profile read/update logic

---

## AI / tooling hints for Copilot sessions

- Prefer reading `hooks.server.ts` and `+layout.ts` together when reasoning about auth flows; they implement the server/client split and cookie handling.
- Changes to auth behavior often require updating both server-side cookie handling and client invalidation logic.
- The project uses `pnpm` by scaffolding but `npm` scripts are present; either package manager works, prefer `pnpm` when available.
